description: A failable function passed as a VALUE (`applyOr(risky, 2)`) whose eventual call is handled where it happens (`f(n) !{ .Empty :> 0 }`) is a clean program: its failability travels with its type (§19.4.3, S469).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "Split + audit" — a failable function MAY be used as a value (passed, returned, stored in a binding); every eventual call is checked
rationale: §19.4.3 (S469): the call `f(n)` inside `applyOr` is a call of a failable function value and is handled by its `!{}`. impl#1 cannot follow a function value to its call and refuses the read `risky` (E-IMPL1-FAILABLE-FN-VALUE) — an impl#1 limitation, carried as g-impl1-failable-fn-value-refused-s469; the bootstrap implements the rule.
